purpose: Defines the criteria and procedure for the additive development workflow used when adding features to an existing project, including feature namespaces, replacement of old specs, and merge.
summary: Concept of a feature as a namespace and the three types: brand-new, purely additive, differential
Requirements and design types are judged per document and may differ
When feature namespaces are needed or unnecessary, and the ban on AI renaming feature names
Applicability: judged by whether spec meaning changes, not by document operation form or change label
Bug fixes are not additive development; exclusion conditions for small changes and red flags
During implementation the additive docs are the current spec; old spec is replaced unconditionally
Design is built from requirements, not bent to existing implementation
Old spec documents are not rewritten during implementation; implementation is not constrained; isolated worktree
Merge definition, scope-based decision of what to move or keep separate, and merge procedure
Frontmatter definition delegated to frontmatter_format as single source of truth

Creating design documents that change existing designs
Deciding whether a change needs a differential feature
Choosing feature names and document placement
Merging additive documents into old specs after implementation
Reviewing documents for additive development compliance
Classifying a defect versus a spec change
title: 追加開発ワークフロー仕様
